description.narrative: Ethiopia is a landlocked country divided into 12 regions and two city administrations. Within these regions, zones, districts, and kebeles are structured for administrative purposes. The country is home to more than eighty ethnic groups and has a population of approximately 120 million people. Of the total population, 50% are female and 50% are male, with an annual population growth rate of 2.6%. About 42% of the population is under 15 years of age. Eighty-three percent of the population lives in rural areas and depend on rainfed agriculture for their livelihoods. Eighty-seven percent of the population is “multidimensionally poor,” suffering from a combination of food insecurity, insufficient access to adequate education and health services, and inadequate employment opportunities. These challenges are exacerbated by climate shocks (mainly drought and floods), conflict, war, insecurity, and disease outbreaks, coupled with a deteriorating economy. Consequently, humanitarian and development situations in almost all parts of Ethiopia are deteriorating. PROGRAMME TITLE / DATE 2 Ethiopia’s humanitarian situation remains concerning, with climate-induced disasters such as drought, floods, and devastating landslides continuing to affect millions of vulnerable Ethiopians, impacting food insecurity and malnutrition. Ongoing conflict and violence, particularly in the Amhara and western Oromia regions, further exacerbate the situation. According to government and inter-agency reports on food security and agriculture (NovDec 2024), the Amhara region has experienced significant production losses, resulting in deteriorating food security in the area. Additionally, internally displaced people (IDPs) hosted in the region require humanitarian relief food assistance. This situation necessitates a timely and appropriate emergency response from the government and humanitarian agencies. The production losses reported from certain areas within some woredas are attributed to excessive dry spells, rainfall, hailstorms, landslides, and frost in both highland and midland regions. Furthermore, the means of income for poor households have been severely affected by internal conflicts, impacting both access to and the price of labor, as well as market access throughout the region. This has adversely affected the income sources of poor and middle-income households. Taking the above into consideration, Cordaid and EOC DICAC have planned a response project through Semi-restricted funds from Cordaid Global office.

The primary objective is to save lives and alleviate the suffering of drought affected people, including children, affected by drought in the Bugna Woreda of the North Wollo Zone in the Amhara region through the provision of primary food assistance over a period of four months. The Specific Objectives is 3050 people affected by the drought are enabled to meet their basic food needs.

The provision of primary food items (wheat flour, pulses/lentils, and food oil) to a total of 3050 drought affected people. This includes children under five years of age, pregnant and lactating mothers, the elderly, and people with disabilities (PWDs)
